claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at the atomic scale.
In situ transmission electron microscopy with heating can investigate nanoparticle thermal behavior at the atomic scale.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are initially in an as-synthesized state.
The nanoparticles can be heated to temperatures up to approximately 1000 K in a controlled environment.
Thermodynamic and kinetic analysis in molecular dynamics simulations can characterize the thermal behavior.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles possess a high-entropy alloy structure.
The constituent elements have different atomic sizes and properties.
Entropy-driven thermodynamic stabilization influences the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Kinetic stabilization influences the thermal behavior of multi-element nanoparticles.
Thermodynamic and kinetic stabilization prevent phase separation in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Thermodynamic and kinetic stabilization prevent elemental segregation in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will exhibit enhanced thermal stability because of their high-entropy alloy structure.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will resist phase separation and elemental segregation at high temperature.
Pure Au or another single-element nanoparticle is the proposed comparison baseline.
The observed behavior is bounded by the temperature range and heating rates used.
The exact thermal-stability mechanisms and the role of each constituent element are not fully understood.
Observation of significant phase separation or elemental segregation at high temperature would falsify the predicted resistance to those changes.
